info.title: AgentDB REST API
info.description: Agent-native operational database. See docs/agent-db.md for design and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md for implementation.

AdminScope.description:
Scope of an admin token — what the bearer is allowed to do.
Checked by the admin-auth middleware against the HTTP
method of the incoming request.

actor_id.description:
Optional agent identifier to attribute this event to. See
`docs/agent-db-v2.md` §2.3 for the agent-as-metadata stance —
free-form string, no pre-registration, no separate resource.

BackupManifest.description:
Metadata written alongside every backup. Identical whether
the backup came from the admin endpoint or the scheduler.

node_id.description: Node id that produced this backup, when available.

out_dir.description: Absolute path to a directory that does NOT yet exist.

BackupSchedulerStatus.description:
Snapshot of the scheduler's recent activity. Surfaced via
`GET /api/admin/backup/status` so operators can answer "when
did the last backup succeed / fail?" without SSHing to the
box.

backups_on_disk.description:
Number of `backup-*` subdirs currently under
`base_dir` (i.e. post-retention count after the last
run).

enabled.description:
`true` when the scheduler is configured and running on
this process (leader-gated; followers report `false`).

last_failure.description: Human-readable reason for the most recent failure.

last_failure_ms.description: Wall-clock ms of the most recent failure.

last_manifest_created_ms.description:
Manifest created_at of the most recent success.
Present iff `last_success_ms` is present.

last_out_dir.description: Path (relative or absolute) of the most recent success.

last_success_ms.description:
Wall-clock ms of the most recent successful run.
`None` before the first success.

last_total_bytes.description: Bytes on disk for the most recent success (kv + meta).

CreateTabletRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/admin/tablets/create` (M25
dynamic tablet creation).

tablet_id.description:
Explicit tablet id. When null, the server picks
`max(existing) + 1` (simple and predictable at
prototype scale).

iterations.description:
PBKDF2 iteration count. Defaults to the RFC floor (4096)
when omitted. Higher values slow down per-auth PBKDF2
work; set for high-security deployments.

password.description:
Plaintext password. Goes through PBKDF2 on the server
and is never persisted. Must be sent over TLS in any
deployment past "localhost dev".

tenant_external.description:
External tenant id this user can access. After SCRAM
handshake completes, this connection is clamped to this
tenant — requests targeting any other tenant are rejected
with 403.

user_id.description:
SCRAM username. Used as both the auth identity and the
stable id for `DELETE /api/admin/users/:user_id`.

DeleteNodeResponse.description:
Body shape for `DELETE /api/admin/nodes/:node_id` responses.
`removed` is `true` when a row matching the path param existed
before the call (so the operator sees the difference between
"id not in table" and "id was already removed in a previous
call").

drained_at_ms.description:
Wall-clock ms of the first drain call on this process, or
`None` before the first call.

is_draining.description: Whether this process is currently draining.

node_id.description:
Node id of this process. `None` for legacy-path registries
(no control plane); those registries can't be drained.

ErrorResponse.description:
The JSON body we emit for every REST error. Always carries
`code`, `type`, `message`; typed extras per code are flat fields.

doc_url.description:
Absolute URL to the runbook for this error code. Present when
the code has a published runbook; omitted otherwise. Operators
should be able to paste this URL into a browser, Slack, or an
incident ticket and land on concrete diagnose/remediate steps.

node_id.description:
Node identifier carried by process-level errors
(`NodeDraining`) so clients can log which specific process
emitted the error when they round-robin across a fleet.

Event.description: An append-only record inside a session.

actor_id.description:
Free-form identifier of the agent that wrote this event. Optional
— not every event is agent-attributable (system events, user
edits, etc.). Indexed at the tablet level for cross-session
retrieval ("all events for agent X"). See `agent-db-v2.md` §2.3.

Agent is a metadata dimension, not a first-class resource: no
registration, no quota, no lifecycle. Promoting this to a full
resource is deferred to v2+ per §10.4.

hlc_ts.description:
Hybrid logical clock timestamp assigned under the session lock at
append time. Gives causality-respecting order across sessions and
tablets. See `agent-db-v2.md` §4 and `hlc.rs`.

ts.description: Unix epoch millis at write time.

ForkRef.description: Reference to a parent session in a fork relationship.

parent_seq_at_fork.description:
Parent's `next_seq` at the moment of fork. The child sees parent events
with `seq < parent_seq_at_fork`.

parent_session_internal_id.description: Parent session's *internal* id (same tenant, same box as the child).

ForkRequest.description:
Body shape for `POST /api/sessions/{session_id}/fork`.

`tenant_id` is **deprecated** as of M26 Phase 1b and will
reject mismatching values when auth is enabled. The
canonical resolution path is now:

1. `AuthedTenant` extension (M26 closeout). When auth is
   enabled, the tenant is taken from credentials and
   cross-checked against the locator.
2. `session_locators::get(parent_session_id)` returns the
   parent's `tenant_external_id`.
3. Body `tenant_id`, kept for back-compat in single-process
   no-auth deployments and the rare pre-locator session.

When several sources supply a tenant and they disagree, the
handler returns 400/403 — silently overruling the client
would hide configuration drift.

tenant_id.description:
Deprecated as of M26 Phase 1b. When omitted, the tenant
is derived from credentials (auth) and/or the parent
session's locator. Supply only for backward compat with
pre-M26 clients in no-auth mode.

HlcStatus.description: Process-global HLC health snapshot, served from `GET /api/admin/hlc`.

max_offset_secs.description:
Configured max-offset window in seconds. Inbound timestamps
whose physical component exceeds `wall + max_offset` are rejected
and counted in `rejects`.

offset_ns.description:
`physical_ns - wall_clock_ns`. Positive when HLC is ahead of wall
(pushed by peers); negative when wall has jumped ahead and HLC
has not yet caught up. Absolute value > a few seconds warrants
investigation.

physical_ns.description: Current HLC physical component (nanoseconds since UNIX epoch).

rejects.description:
Running count of inbound timestamps rejected by the max-offset
guard. Any non-zero value is a signal; a sustained growth rate
indicates a clock-skew problem or a rogue peer.

wall_clock_ns.description:
Local wall clock at the time of this snapshot, nanoseconds since
epoch. Compare against `physical_ns` to estimate `offset_ns`.

HlcTimestamp.description:
A hybrid logical clock timestamp.

Encoded as 12 bytes on the wire: an 8-byte physical component
(nanoseconds since UNIX epoch) and a 4-byte logical counter that breaks
ties when the physical component does not advance between events.

logical.description:
Tie-breaker counter. Incremented when two events land in the same
physical nanosecond.

physical_ns.description:
Nanoseconds since UNIX epoch. Tracks wall-clock time with
causality-respecting floors enforced on `update()`.

last_sample_ms.description:
Wall-clock ms of the last detector sample. Zero when
this node isn't the scheduler leader.

is_live.description:
True when `expires_at_ms > now_ms` at the moment of the read.
A `false` here on a long-quiet cluster indicates either the
last leader died without a successor acquiring, or the
`lease_duration` is large compared to read cadence.

description.description:
Free-form label so operators can tell tokens apart.
Shown in the list endpoint; never used for auth.

oneOf.description:
RBAC scope: `admin` (default) or `readonly`. Readonly
tokens can only issue GET requests against
`/api/admin/*`; every other method returns 403.

scope.description: RBAC scope of the minted token.

availability_zone.description:
Availability zone declared via `AGENTDB_NODE_AZ`. `None`
for single-AZ deployments and pre-migration-013 nodes.
Tablet placement prefers cross-AZ targets when this is
populated for two or more nodes.

is_stale.description:
True when this node's last heartbeat is older than the
configured `stale_threshold_ms` (default 15000). Diagnostic —
the scheduler that M22 will add does the actual failover
decision; this flag is just for operator visibility.

mongo_address.description:
Mongo wire listener address advertised for cross-node
forwarding. `None` when the node predates migration
008 or didn't set `AGENTDB_NODE_MONGO_ADDRESS`.

reloaded_at_ms.description: Wall-clock ms when the reload completed.

slow_query_threshold_ms.description: Current slow-query threshold in ms, post-reload.

tenant_quotas_added.description:
Tenants whose quota was added in this reload (new
rows in the meta table since the last hydration).

tenant_quotas_removed.description:
Tenants whose quota was removed (deleted from the
meta table since the last hydration).

tracing_filter.description:
Current tracing filter string, post-reload. Empty
when no filter change was applied.

oneOf.description:
Canonical leader row from the control plane. `None` means no
leader has ever been elected on this cluster.

nodes_gc_removed_total.description:
Total long-dead node rows this process has GC'd from the
meta table as leader.

nodes_marked_dead_total.description:
Total `alive -> dead` node transitions this process has
performed as leader. Same leader-gated semantics as
`reassignments_total`.

reassignments_total.description:
Total number of tablet leases this process has cleared as
part of the stale-lease reaper sweep. Only advances while
this process is the leader — followers report 0 even if
another node in the cluster has reaped many leases.

tablet_handoffs_completed_total.description:
Total cooperative handoffs this process has completed
as a source — observed a `handoff_target_node_id` set
on a tablet it owned, drained, and atomically
transferred ownership. Per-node counter (every node
reports its own); add up across the cluster to count
total handoffs end-to-end.

tablet_placements_total.description:
Total tablet placements made by this process while
leader (`owner_node_id` NULL → some alive node). Same
leader-gated semantics; followers report 0.

tablet_rebalances_total.description:
Total cooperative handoffs this process has signalled
while leader (rebalance pass writes
`handoff_target_node_id` on a tablet). Doubles as an
SLO signal: a leader inflicting many handoffs per
minute means the cluster has chronic load drift.

this_node_epoch.description:
Current epoch observed by this process's election loop. Zero
before the first acquire attempt completes.

this_node_id.description: Node id this process registered as.

this_node_is_leader.description:
`true` if this process's `LeaderElection::is_leader()` says
so. Derived from the last successful acquire/renew — may be
up to `renew_interval` stale after a loss of leadership, but
never falsely `true` past `lease_duration`.

primary_agent_id.description:
The primary agent that owns this session, if single-agent. Multi-
agent sessions (orchestrator + workers) may leave this unset and
disambiguate at the event level via `Event::actor_id`. Indexed
for cross-session queries. See `agent-db-v2.md` §2.3.

segment_path.description: When `tier == Cold`, the `object_store` path where events live. None for warm sessions.

SetShardRequest.description:
Body for `POST /api/admin/shards/:id`. `tablet_id: null` reverts
the shard to default (hash) routing; a set value pins it.

last_refresh_ms.description:
Wall-clock ms of the last successful refresh from meta; if
the shown `tablet_id` is stale, it's never more stale than
`refresh_interval` seconds.

session_id.description:
If the caller provided `?session_id=...`, echo it back so
scripts and the CLI can correlate.

shard_id.description: Shard id the request resolved to.

tablet_id.description:
Tablet currently assigned to this shard. `null` means "no
override — routing falls back to the default (hash % num
boxes) rule the client should already know about".

ShardOverridesList.description:
Response for `GET /api/admin/shards/list`. Only shards with an
explicit assignment are returned — 16384 rows is too many for a
human-scale listing.

fraction.description:
Fraction of the source's currently-overridden shards to
move. Clamped to (0, 1]. Defaults to 0.5 (half).

migrate_data.description:
When true, after reassigning the shards the server
enumerates sessions on the source tablet whose shard
is in the moved set and migrates each warm one to
the destination via
[`agentdb_core::migrate_warm_session`]. Cold/archive
sessions are reported in `skipped_sessions` and
otherwise left alone. Default false for backward
compatibility (previous callers don't expect data to
move).

to_tablet_id.description:
Target tablet to move shards to. When `null`, the server
picks the least-loaded tablet from the detector's
snapshot (excluding the source).

migrated_sessions.description:
Sessions whose warm state was rekeyed to the dest
tablet. Only populated when `migrate_data == true`.

skipped_sessions.description:
Sessions on the moved shards that the migration
refused (cold / archive / fork parent). Operators
handle these out of band.

SlowQueryKind.description:
What kind of request this record describes. Used for
filtering in the admin endpoint and as a label on the
recorded-count counter.

detail.description:
Short request summary. For append this is the
payload byte size; for find/aggregate it's a
truncated filter/pipeline BSON excerpt. Never
includes secrets — callers are responsible for the
redaction boundary.

id.description:
Monotonically-increasing id assigned at record time.
Exposed so clients can page via `after_id` without
fighting timestamp ties.

session_id.description:
Session or collection identifier, if the request
carries one. Find/aggregate on an unscoped tenant
leaves this empty.

tenant_id.description: External tenant id (the URL path segment).

ts_ms.description: Wall-clock ms when the request completed.

epoch.description:
Monotonic counter that bumps on every successful ownership
change; used as the fencing token on storage-path writes
(follow-up PR wires that).

lease_expires_at_ms.description:
Wall-clock ms at which the current lease expires. `0` when the
tablet has never been claimed.

owner_node_id.description:
Node id currently holding the lease, if any. `None` means the
tablet row exists but has never been claimed.

deny_count.description:
Running count of denials this process has served for
this tenant since the bucket was (re)configured. Not
persisted — resets on restart. Operators watching
`agentdb_tenant_quota_denies_total{tenant="..."}` on
`/metrics` get the same number across restarts.

updated_at_ms.description: Wall-clock ms when the quota was last set via PUT.

UserListItem.description:
Response envelope for `GET /api/admin/users`. Wraps
`users::UserSummary` so utoipa can generate a schema without
making the meta crate depend on utoipa.
